subject: Week 50: first dental visit by age 1 — the AAP deadline is May 11
bodyText:
This week
Walking confidence grows for those already stepping while others cruise and stand — both on track across the 9–15+ month range (CDC walks-alone checkpoint: 15 months: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). He now uses objects as tools to extend his reach and imitates increasingly elaborate actions — stirring, phone-to-ear, brushing. The gesture repertoire is rich; words besides mama and dada remain emerging for some, with the CDC checkpoint at 15 months.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Day-to-day food intake swinging 40% in either direction — normal at this age; judge the week, not the meal.
- [low concern] Stranger wariness intensifying — expected 12-month social development, not regression.
- [monitor] No single words plus minimal babble plus limited response to his name — document the combination and raise it at the 12-month visit.
- [call within 24h] New rash within 2 hours of a new food, without any breathing involvement — stop the food and call.
- [call now] Fever 102F rectal or higher with lethargy, or hives with facial swelling or breathing difficulty — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Narrate your daily walk and name everything he points to — point-then-label is the highest-yield language input available right now, and conversational turns, not raw word count, predict later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Keep one weekly participatory music class, or daily singing at home — same active ingredient. Active music beat passive listening on rhythm discrimination and prelinguistic gesture in the one randomized trial at this age; one class is plenty. Gerry, Unrau and Trainor 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Put swim on the year-2 calendar: AAP endorses formal lessons from age 1, which is when the drowning-risk-reduction evidence actually begins — one weekly class, no stacking. AAP — swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx
- Load meals with iron ahead of the 12-month hemoglobin check — meat, lentils, and iron-fortified cereal with a vitamin C pairing. Iron deficiency peaks at 9–24 months, and excess milk crowding out iron-rich solids is the usual mechanism.

Upcoming
- By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — AAP recommends by age 1 or within 6 months of the first tooth, whichever comes first.
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — the largest vaccine round of year one (MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster) plus hemoglobin and lead screen; confirm the slot.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — final headcount and food orders next week; keep the party window anchored to naps.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Shows you an object she likes
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Joint attention with intention to share — distinct from pointing to request. Strong autism-screen marker when consistently absent.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/shows-object-she-likes/complete

- Follows directions given with a gesture and words
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Combined verbal + nonverbal cues. Pure-verbal compliance comes after.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/follows-gesture-plus-words/complete

- Copies other children while playing
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Peer-directed imitation, not just imitation of parents.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/copies-other-children/complete

- Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Pretend nurture — early symbolic play. Often emerges with a favorite lovey.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hugs-stuffed-toy/complete

- Stacks at least two small objects (like blocks)
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Visuomotor coordination + planning. Knocking the stack down is also part of the practice.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stacks-two-objects/complete
